page: Microsoft Azure D2a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provides two dedicated virtual CPUs backed by a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading (two threads per core). The compute setup is supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, FMA, and BMI2.

Memory provisioning stands at 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes equipped with 54 GB of local temporary SSD storage. It features zero bundled GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization hypervisor.

Benchmark data displays a contrast between single-threaded execution and aggregate throughput. Single-core stress-ng CPU performance ranks within the top 25 percent, while single-core Geekbench text processing and gzip compression scores align with the middle 50 percent of tested cloud servers. However, because total processing capacity is restricted to two vCPUs across one physical core, multi-core benchmarks show clear scale constraints. The multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU metrics sit in the lower 25 percent, and multi-core Geekbench tasks like clang software compilation and image processing fall into the bottom 10 percent. Measured memory bandwidth and Redis SET throughput similarly reflect entry-level bandwidth profiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2a_v4 offers an entry-tier general-purpose footprint with dedicated vCPU allocation and included fast local SSD scratch space. Tradeoffs center on low aggregate multi-core throughput and limited parallel I/O capacity. The instance is suited for lightweight workloads that benefit from solid single-core frequency but do not require heavy parallelization, such as entry-level web hosting, small background workers, automated testing tasks, and low-traffic staging environments.

Configured with two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading, it includes 8.0 GB of RAM and 54 GB of local temporary SSD storage. Its x86_64 instruction set supports AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI extensions. Performance benchmarks indicate respectable single-core output, with stress-ng single-core execution scoring in the top 25 percent. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics, memory bandwidth, and database transaction throughput fall into lower percentiles due to the limited two-thread core count. The instance does not include a GPU or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and bundled local solid-state storage, the D2a_v4 is best suited for entry-level general workloads, small web serving instances, code building tasks, and lightweight development environments.
